chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Every intoxicant from the drinks obligates the penalty (Hadd) with regards to it, just as it obligates regarding the wine.

key_terms.الْحَدِّ: The fixed corporal punishment prescribed by Sharia
key_terms.الْخَمْرِ: Wine; the primary reference for intoxication in fiqh

ai.seo_question: What is the legal penalty for consuming any intoxicating drink according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'idtirar' (intoxication) as the effective cause for the Hadd penalty, extending the corporal punishment for wine to all intoxicating substances regardless of their source. It serves as a foundational text in Shia jurisprudence for deriving rulings on modern intoxicants by linking them to the primary Quranic prohibition of Khamr.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Noman, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kanany, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Every intoxicant from the drinks Obligates the Penalty (Hadd) with regards to it, just as it Obligates regarding the wine’.
